answer: A durable defence is stake-bound reputation: an agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and each verified action adds to a public ledger. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, and one proven fraud slashes the whole stake. Think of each identity as a marble balanced on a ridge: cheap to roll down into the crowd, costly to climb back after a slash. A cipher-signed history ties every action to its stake, so cheap talk cannot buy trust; only costly, checkable behaviour can.
